title: A cp of another agent's scratchpad file keeps that agent as writer
why: Decision scratchpad-owner: an agent runs only its own copy 'made from a read of it'; its remedy says read, then write an own copy. #2830 (case cp-mv 3 in tests/guard/s34371-scratchpad-owner.py) lets agent B cp agent A's script and run the copy, and its remedy text steers B to cp. That skips the read the decision exists for. Expected harm: B runs a script it never read, which is the guard's incident class, and the remedy itself teaches the bypass.
source: triage 03:08 CST Nov 13, reconciling the coordinator's 16:45 CST Nov 12 step-note settlement with decision scratchpad-owner (coordinator 03:07 CST)
note: Fix: B's cp of A's file records A as writer, as the debt scratchpad-owner-cp-mv-dest already says for mv; case cp-mv 3 flips to refused (red first); the remedy names read-then-write, never cp. Why the decision wins over the 16:45 settlement: that settlement cited building-port-keeps-behaviour, which keeps a port's behaviour, while main's cp pass is a listed ceiling of the guard (decision line 26), not chosen behaviour. #2830 and #3013 merge as they are (coordinator, process-only): no hole opens against main. Guard change: a lane, red first. Undo: say so and the lane drops the step. 07:33 CST Nov 13: lane session_013NEJL2sGyAvwpHNCHioxLc, PR #3126 (head cb15b3758). Its question: recording A as writer of B's cp also refuses B's own retry, edit or rm of the copy, which main allows. Triage pick (b) in a smaller form: the same sidecar adds a copier key. A run reads the writer; overwrite and rm/mv treat the copier as the owner. Option (a) would ship a known false alarm (decision scratchpad-owner, false-alarm sentences). Undo: coordinator or owner says (a) and the lane takes (a). #3126 at 10d984931: record done (rounds 1 to 3, net positive), but lane lint reads unknown because no touched-tests run exists on its head. Owner act posted as Cockpit item 692 (type --lint-unknown-ok in the lane) at 10:48 CST Nov 13. Cause: step draft-push-starts-touched-run.
